title: Shortening induction time with simultaneous use of Dilapan-S and misoprostol compared with conventional labor induction in women with an unfavorable cervix.
summary:
Background
In some cases, it is necessary to start labor artificially. This process can take a long time, especially when the cervix is not yet sufficiently prepared for childbirth. There are different methods to support the opening of the cervix and to initiate labor. These include the use of medication to stimulate contractions, as well as mechanical rods that slowly widen the cervix by absorbing fluid. It is not yet sufficiently clear whether combining these methods can shorten the time until labor begins and until the baby is born.
Research question
Can the combination of two methods of labor induction shorten the time until the onset of labor and until the birth of the baby compared with the conventional method using medication alone?
Methods
Pregnant women who require labor induction will receive either the combined method or a medication-only method. The time from the start of labor induction to the onset of labor, as well as to the birth of the baby, will be measured. The progress of labor induction will be monitored using ultrasound examinations and vaginal examinations. In addition, participants will be asked to complete an online questionnaire before and after birth to assess their satisfaction with the labor induction process.

interventions.name: Simultaneous use of Dilapan-S (rods), with insertion of 1–3 rods once daily into the cervical canal at 24-hour intervals, and misoprostol (tablets) up to 4 times daily at 50 µg per dose (maximum daily dose 200 µg) until the onset of labor.
Misoprostol (tablets) up to 4 times daily at 50 µg per dose (maximum daily dose 200 µg) until the onset of labor.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Indication for labor induction
- 37+0 to 41+0 weeks of gestation
- Singleton pregnancy
- Cephalic presentation
Exclusion criteria:
- Placenta previa 
- Multiple pregnancy
- Breech presentation
- Suspected intra-amniotic infection
- Premature rupture of membranes
- Positive vaginal swab for Group B streptococci
- Previous cesarean section or uterine surgery
